lab.title: Centralize and verify dependency injection registration
lab.objective: Identify Web Program.cs as the composition root.
lab.task: Add AddTimeClockPersistence, use it from Web, and prove AsyncClockEntryService resolves inside a scope.
lab.startingCondition: Session 33 composed EF Core and AsyncClockEntryService directly in the Web host. Session 34 extracts those actual registrations and verifies constructor resolution.

steps.text: Step 1/12: In Infrastructure, create ServiceRegistration.cs and declare public static class ServiceRegistration.
Step 2/12: Inside it, add AddTimeClockPersistence extending IServiceCollection and accepting a SQLite connection string.
Step 3/12: Inside AddTimeClockPersistence, call AddDbContext<TimeClockDbContext> with UseSqlite(connectionString).
Step 4/12: Register IAsyncClockEntryRepository to EfClockEntryRepository with AddScoped.
Step 5/12: Register AsyncClockEntryService with AddScoped and return the same IServiceCollection.
Step 6/12: Signature reminder: AddScoped<TService,TImplementation> maps the requested interface to one implementation reused inside one scope.
Step 7/12: In Web/Program.cs, replace the individual persistence registrations with AddTimeClockPersistence. Program.cs remains the composition root choosing the connection string.
Step 8/12: Build Web in Release before adding the resolution test.
Step 9/12: In the test project, create ServiceRegistrationTests.cs and build a ServiceCollection with AddTimeClockPersistence.
Step 10/12: Build the provider, create one scope, and resolve AsyncClockEntryService with GetRequiredService.
Step 11/12: Assert the resolved service is not null. Constructor injection must transitively resolve its repository and DbContext.
Step 12/12: Run ServiceRegistrationTests, start Web to verify resolution, then build the solution and run all tests with --no-build.

reveals.title: Solution
reveals.text: The registration extension owns the actual scoped persistence graph.
